cues: In front of a crowd of doctors, a dentist named William Morton holds a glass globe to a patient's mouth.
The patient breathes in a sweet smelling vapour, falls asleep, and a tumour is cut from his neck without a cry of pain.
The vapour was ether, and surgery was changed forever.
text: Boston, October eighteen forty six. In front of a crowd of doctors, a dentist named William Morton holds a glass globe to a patient's mouth. The patient breathes in a sweet smelling vapour, falls asleep, and a tumour is cut from his neck without a cry of pain. The vapour was ether, and surgery was changed forever.
